items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03
items.q: But Mama didn't, you didn't stay over there all the time because I was born then and Mama used to be here every month or so.

ctx.x: Yeah, in the storm we come here. In this storm right at Washington and Ramport. We come here from Moluccio in that storm.

But Mama didn't, you didn't stay over there all the time because I was born then and Mama used to be here every month or so. I mean, we weren't living here but we used to be here all the time. Because I was born then and I know I had been here I don't know how many times during that time. When you mean we come to live? I know when we came back to live. I know when we came back to live but I mean you made I guess hundreds of visits. Oh yes, right. Yeah. Because you visit over here quite often.
When did they start playing jazz and Mobile?

items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: Yeah. I was there, and I know what some of them when I was there had.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, yeah. Uh-huh. I have, uh, oh, I have a collection of records in Chicago. I still have my house in Chicago. I got all Bessie Smith, Manny Smith, Clara Smith, I got all her records. I, I'm sure I have some of Punch's records. I, I don't know, but I have, uh, a lot of old records that I had just put in the box and put aside as I get new ones. I have some old records, I guess, 25 or 30 some years old there. Please come out. I got to see that.
Yeah. I was there, and I know what some of them when I was there had.

Yeah, I have, uh, boxes of records. I, we had a phonograph since 1920. We got, we had one here. Mm-hmm. And then when I went to Chicago, I, I, is there, every, my thing improved? I improved with it. I had one of those that you turn, you know how you turn. Mm-hmm. And when the other electric came out, I had one of those.
